curriculumDefinition.commandsAndConcepts: `i I a A o O`; `x X`; `r R`; `s S`; `J gJ`; `u`, `Ctrl-r`; `~`, `g~`, `gu`, `gU`; `Ctrl-a`, `Ctrl-x`
curriculumDefinition.learningOutcome: Choose a precise entry/change command, undo safely, and perform common local transformations
curriculumDefinition.representativeExercises: Append an argument; open a line; replace a delimiter; join a wrapped statement; change case; increment a version number
curriculumDefinition.priorityAndPortability: Core, with `R`, `gJ`, and numeric changes introduced after the everyday commands

lessons.title: Enter text exactly where it belongs
lessons.objective: Choose i, I, a, or A from the intended insertion boundary.

activities.title: Before, after, first text, or line end
activities.body: `i` inserts before the cursor and `a` appends after it. Their uppercase partners target line landmarks: `I` starts at the first nonblank character and `A` starts at the physical line end.
activities.grammar: i → before · a → after · I → first text · A → line end
activities.contrast: Choose the boundary directly instead of moving there one character at a time.

activities.title: Frame an assignment
activities.instruction: Insert `const ` before the first text, then append a semicolon at the line end.

commandGroups.explanation: Enter Insert mode at the first nonblank and add the declaration keyword.
Append punctuation at the physical end and return to Normal mode.

feedback.success: The declaration was framed without navigation taps.
feedback.why: I targeted the first text while A targeted the line end.

provenance.languageRationale: An indented JavaScript assignment exposes both first-text and line-end entry points.

activities.title: Insert before the value
activities.instruction: Insert `4` before the final digit to make `42`.

commandGroups.explanation: Insert immediately before the cursor, then return to Normal mode.

hints: The new digit belongs before the cursor.

feedback.success: The number became 42.
feedback.why: i opened Insert mode on the cursor's left boundary.

provenance.languageRationale: A short Python assignment makes the insertion boundary unambiguous.

activities.title: Append after an item
activities.instruction: Append a comma after `1` without moving onto the following space.

commandGroups.explanation: Append on the cursor's right boundary.

hints: The punctuation belongs after the selected item.

feedback.success: The list separator is in place.
feedback.why: a began text entry directly after the 1.

provenance.languageRationale: A compact list gives append-after a natural punctuation task.

activities.title: Finish the statement
activities.instruction: Append a semicolon at the end of the line from the current distant cursor.

commandGroups.explanation: Jump to the end and append in one entry command.

hints: Do not walk to the line end.

feedback.success: The statement is terminated.
feedback.why: A combined line-end movement with entry.

provenance.languageRationale: A JavaScript return statement naturally needs terminal punctuation.

lessons.title: Create space above or below
lessons.objective: Use o and O to open a correctly placed new line and begin typing.

activities.title: Open below or above
activities.body: `o` creates a new line below the current row; `O` creates one above. Both enter Insert mode immediately so the new row can be filled without a separate command.
activities.grammar: o → open below · O → open above
activities.contrast: Opening a line is one change, not a movement followed by Enter.

activities.title: Fill the missing call
activities.instruction: Open a line below `first()` and type `second()`.

commandGroups.explanation: Open below, enter the call, and return to Normal mode.

feedback.success: The call sequence now has its middle row.
feedback.why: o created the row and entered Insert mode as one command.

activities.portability: Indentation is intentionally neutral; host autoindent settings can vary.

provenance.languageRationale: Three top-level calls avoid host-specific indentation while giving the new line a clear position.

activities.title: Insert the missing label
activities.instruction: Open a row above `gamma` and type `beta`.

commandGroups.explanation: Open above the current row and fill it.

hints: The new row belongs above the cursor.

feedback.success: The labels are ordered.
feedback.why: O opened a row above gamma.

provenance.languageRationale: A neutral YAML-like list isolates vertical placement without indentation rules.

activities.title: Navigate, then open above
activities.instruction: Jump to the final row, open above it, and type `middle`.

commandGroups.explanation: Reach the final logical line.
Open above it and enter the missing row.

feedback.success: The middle row landed between the endpoints.
feedback.why: G chose the anchor row and O created space above it.

provenance.languageRationale: Directional labels make row order immediately readable.

activities.title: Frame a small block
activities.instruction: Open `header` above the block, then `footer` below its final row.

commandGroups.explanation: Create the header above.
Reach the final row.
Create the footer below.

hints: Use uppercase above and lowercase below.
Jump to the last row between the changes.

feedback.success: The block now has both boundaries.
feedback.why: O and o expressed opposite insertion directions directly.

provenance.languageRationale: A neutral block keeps the challenge about placement rather than syntax.

lessons.title: Delete or replace the smallest target
lessons.objective: Use x, X, and r for local character corrections without entering a longer edit.

activities.title: Remove here, remove before, or replace
activities.body: `x` deletes the character under the cursor, while `X` deletes the character before it. `r{char}` replaces one character and stays in Normal mode.
activities.grammar: x → delete here · X → delete before · r{char} → replace here
activities.contrast: Use `r` when the target width is already exactly one character.

activities.title: Repair three tiny defects
activities.instruction: Delete a duplicate colon, replace the final character with a semicolon, then remove one leading hash with X.

commandGroups.explanation: Delete the duplicate colon under the cursor.
Reach the next row's final character.
Replace that one character without entering Insert mode.
Stand after the extra hash and delete backward.

feedback.success: All three one-character defects are gone.
feedback.why: x, r, and X matched the defect direction and width.

provenance.languageRationale: Log-like rows make isolated punctuation defects visually obvious.

activities.title: Remove a fixed run
activities.instruction: Delete the three trailing `x` characters with a count.

commandGroups.explanation: Delete three characters starting under the cursor.

hints: The unwanted run starts under the cursor.

feedback.success: The suffix is clean.
feedback.why: The count made x cover the known three-character width.

provenance.languageRationale: A neutral token isolates counted character deletion.

activities.title: Delete backward
activities.instruction: Remove the extra slash immediately before the cursor.

commandGroups.explanation: Delete the character immediately before the cursor.

hints: The unwanted character is left of the cursor.

feedback.success: The path has one separator.
feedback.why: X deletes backward without a separate left motion.

provenance.languageRationale: A doubled path separator gives X a realistic local correction.

activities.title: Repair one letter
activities.instruction: Replace `q` with `u` without entering Insert mode.

commandGroups.explanation: Replace exactly the character under the cursor.

feedback.success: The boolean is repaired.
feedback.why: r performed a one-for-one replacement and stayed in Normal mode.

provenance.languageRationale: A misspelled boolean makes the one-character replacement meaningful.

lessons.title: Replace one unit or keep overwriting
lessons.objective: Choose s, S, or R according to the replacement span.

activities.title: Character, line, or overwrite stream
activities.body: `s` removes the character under the cursor and enters Insert mode; `S` replaces the whole line. `R` enters Replace mode, overwriting existing characters until the line ends and then inserting beyond it.
activities.grammar: s → substitute character · S → substitute line · R → overwrite stream
activities.contrast: Use the smallest command whose replacement span matches the task.

activities.title: Overwrite a fixed-width value
activities.instruction: Enter Replace mode on `oldxx` and overwrite it with `draft`.

commandGroups.explanation: Overwrite the existing five-character value and return to Normal mode.

feedback.success: The old value was overwritten in place.
feedback.why: R replaced existing characters instead of shifting them right.

provenance.languageRationale: Equal-width state labels make overwrite semantics immediately visible.

activities.title: Substitute a character
activities.instruction: Replace the `x` in `hxgh` with `i` using s.

commandGroups.explanation: Remove one character, enter its replacement, and leave Insert mode.

feedback.success: The level now reads high.
feedback.why: s combined a one-character deletion with Insert mode.

provenance.languageRationale: A short string value gives s an obvious one-character correction.

activities.title: Replace a placeholder row
activities.instruction: Replace the entire `TODO` line with `return true;`.

commandGroups.explanation: Substitute the complete current line and type its replacement.

hints: Replace it in one Insert session.

feedback.success: The placeholder became a real statement.
feedback.why: S selected the whole logical line as the replacement unit.

activities.portability: The fixture is unindented because automatic indentation is host-configurable.

provenance.languageRationale: A top-level placeholder avoids host-specific indentation while preserving a realistic line replacement.

activities.title: Overwrite and extend
activities.instruction: Use Replace mode to turn `dev` into `production`, continuing beyond the old line end.

commandGroups.explanation: Overwrite the old value, then insert once Replace mode reaches the line end.

hints: The replacement starts at the cursor and is longer than the old value.

feedback.success: The tag was replaced and extended.
feedback.why: Replace mode overwrote dev, then inserted the remaining characters at end-of-line.

provenance.languageRationale: A deployment tag naturally demonstrates a longer replacement value.

lessons.title: Recover and reapply safely
lessons.objective: Use u and Ctrl-r to inspect, undo, and restore complete changes.

activities.title: Undo a change; redo an undo
activities.body: `u` reverses the most recent complete change. `Ctrl-r` reapplies an undone change. An Insert or Replace session should undo as one unit, not one typed character at a time.
activities.contrast: Reset restarts an exercise; undo stays inside the edit history.

activities.title: Test and restore punctuation
activities.instruction: Append a semicolon, undo the complete append, then redo it.

commandGroups.explanation: Create one complete append change.
Undo that whole change.
Redo the undone change.

feedback.success: The append survived an undo-and-redo check.
feedback.why: History treated the complete Insert session as one change.

provenance.languageRationale: Terminal punctuation makes the history state visible after every step.

activities.title: Undo a deletion
activities.instruction: Delete the final extra `e`, then undo that deletion.

commandGroups.explanation: Delete the selected character.
Restore it from history.

feedback.success: The deletion was reversed.
feedback.why: u restored the exact prior buffer state.

provenance.languageRationale: A duplicated letter makes deletion and restoration obvious.

activities.title: Restore a substitution
activities.instruction: Change `l` to `r`, undo the Insert session, then redo it.

commandGroups.explanation: Create one substitution change.
Undo the substitution.
Redo it.

hints: Complete the substitution before inspecting history.
u moves backward; Ctrl-r moves forward.

feedback.success: The corrected word was restored.
feedback.why: Ctrl-r replayed the complete substitution that u had reversed.

provenance.languageRationale: A one-letter word correction makes the history round trip easy to audit.

activities.title: Verify before keeping a change
activities.instruction: Append a semicolon, undo it to inspect the prior state, then redo it.

commandGroups.explanation: Make the append.
Inspect the prior state.
Keep the change by redoing it.

hints: Walk backward once, then forward once.

feedback.success: The checked change remains applied.
feedback.why: Undo and redo let you inspect history without rebuilding the edit.

provenance.languageRationale: A concise state assignment provides a realistic punctuation check.

lessons.title: Join lines with deliberate spacing
lessons.objective: Use J or gJ according to whether boundary whitespace should be normalized or preserved.

activities.title: Normalize or preserve the join
activities.body: `J` joins the next logical line, trims its indentation, and inserts one separating space when needed. `gJ` removes only the newline, preserving the surrounding spaces exactly.
activities.grammar: J → normalized join · gJ → whitespace-preserving join
activities.contrast: Visible whitespace matters when choosing between these commands.

activities.title: Compare both join boundaries
activities.instruction: Join the first statement with J, move down, then join the second statement with gJ.

commandGroups.explanation: Normalize the first boundary to one space.
Move to the next broken statement.
Remove only its newline and preserve the spaces.

feedback.success: The two boundaries expose both spacing policies.
feedback.why: J normalized indentation; gJ preserved every space around the removed newline.

activities.portability: Core Vim behavior; whitespace visualization is instructional only.

provenance.languageRationale: Two broken JavaScript statements make normalized and preserved spacing directly comparable.

activities.title: Reconnect the broken statement
activities.instruction: Join the two source lines with one uppercase command.

commandGroups.explanation: Join the next line and normalize its indentation.

hints: Use the join that cleans indentation.

feedback.success: The statement flows across one line.
feedback.why: J removed the newline and normalized the boundary to one space.

provenance.languageRationale: The prototype aqueduct statement remains a natural introductory J exercise.

activities.title: Keep the exact gap
activities.instruction: Remove the newline while preserving the existing spaces around it.

commandGroups.explanation: Remove only the newline and preserve all three boundary spaces.

hints: A normal J would collapse this gap.

feedback.success: The exact three-space gap remains.
feedback.why: gJ preserved whitespace instead of normalizing it.

activities.portability: Core Vim behavior; spaces are visualized because they are the evidence.

provenance.languageRationale: A neutral key/value row makes preserved whitespace measurable.

activities.title: Join adjacent arguments
activities.instruction: Join the `one` and `two` argument rows while keeping the closing delimiter separate.

commandGroups.explanation: Join only the current row with its successor.

hints: Only the next newline should disappear.
Whitespace should normalize around the join.

feedback.success: The two arguments now share a row.
feedback.why: J joined exactly the current and next logical lines.

provenance.languageRationale: A multi-line call makes the selected join boundary structurally meaningful.

lessons.title: Change case without retyping
lessons.objective: Use ~ and the g-prefixed case operators to toggle, lowercase, or uppercase a motion range.

activities.title: Toggle one or transform a range
activities.body: `~` toggles the character under the cursor and advances. `g~`, `gu`, and `gU` wait for a motion, then toggle, lowercase, or uppercase that range.
activities.grammar: ~ → toggle char · g~{motion} → toggle · gu{motion} → lower · gU{motion} → upper
activities.contrast: The g-prefixed forms reuse known motions without introducing the general operator families from the next unit.

activities.title: Capitalize and emphasize
activities.instruction: Toggle the first letter of `draft`, move to `ready`, then uppercase that word.

commandGroups.explanation: Toggle one character and advance.
Move to the next word.
Uppercase through the word motion.

feedback.success: The sentence has title case and emphasis.
feedback.why: ~ handled one character; gUw transformed a motion-sized range.

provenance.languageRationale: Two plain words clearly expose character toggle and word-range uppercase.

activities.title: Normalize an uppercase word
activities.instruction: Lowercase `ERROR` through the next word boundary.

commandGroups.explanation: Lowercase the range covered by w.

feedback.success: The log level is lowercase.
feedback.why: gu applied lowercasing to the w range.

provenance.languageRationale: A log level is a natural case-normalization target.

activities.title: Invert mixed case
activities.instruction: Toggle every letter in `mIxEd` using a word motion.

commandGroups.explanation: Toggle the case of the w range.

hints: Use the g-prefixed toggle with w.

feedback.success: Every letter inverted case.
feedback.why: g~ composed toggle-case with the word motion.

provenance.languageRationale: A deliberately mixed word makes every toggled character observable.

activities.title: Apply opposite case transforms
activities.instruction: Uppercase `public`, move forward, then lowercase `DRAFT`.

commandGroups.explanation: Uppercase the first word.
Move to the second word.
Lowercase the second word.

hints: Use the same motion with two opposite operators.
Uppercase first, then move one word.

feedback.success: Both words now follow their requested styles.
feedback.why: gU and gu reused the same word motion for opposite transformations.

provenance.languageRationale: Contrasting words make the two case policies easy to inspect.

lessons.title: Increment or decrement numbers in place
lessons.objective: Use Ctrl-a and Ctrl-x, with optional counts, for local decimal changes.

activities.title: Add or subtract without retyping
activities.body: `Ctrl-a` increments the number at or after the cursor; `Ctrl-x` decrements it. A count supplies the amount, making small version and retry changes precise.
activities.grammar: count? + Ctrl-a → add · count? + Ctrl-x → subtract
activities.contrast: These lessons use decimal values; alternate numeric formats are outside this unit.

activities.title: Raise a version and lower retries
activities.instruction: Add three to version 7, move to retries, then subtract one.

commandGroups.explanation: Add three to the first number.
Move through the label to the next number.
Subtract one from retries.

feedback.success: Both numeric settings changed in place.
feedback.why: The count scaled Ctrl-a while Ctrl-x used its default amount of one.

activities.portability: Core decimal Vim behavior; host nrformats settings may affect other formats.

provenance.languageRationale: A compact settings row makes two decimal changes easy to compare.

activities.title: Advance the version
activities.instruction: Increment version 19 to 20.

commandGroups.explanation: Add one to the decimal number at the cursor.

feedback.success: The version advanced to 20.
feedback.why: Ctrl-a incremented the complete decimal token.

provenance.languageRationale: A version value is the canonical practical increment task.

activities.title: Reduce retries by two
activities.instruction: Subtract two from the retry count.

commandGroups.explanation: Use a count to subtract two.

hints: Supply the amount before the chord.

feedback.success: The retry count is now three.
feedback.why: The count changed Ctrl-x from minus one to minus two.

provenance.languageRationale: A retry limit is a natural small decrement.

activities.title: Reach and advance a build
activities.instruction: From the line start, reach the final number and add two.

commandGroups.explanation: Reach the final digit.
Add two to the complete decimal token.

hints: Use a known line landmark first.

feedback.success: Build 40 became 42.
feedback.why: Ctrl-a found the numeric token even from its final digit.

provenance.languageRationale: A build number provides a realistic counted increment after movement.

lessons.title: Choose the smallest precise change
lessons.objective: Combine entry, joining, case, numeric, and history commands according to editing intent.

activities.title: Let the target shape choose the command
activities.body: Choose an entry command from the boundary, a character command from the defect width, a join from its whitespace policy, and a case or numeric transform when retyping would discard structure.
activities.contrast: The shortest useful command is the one whose behavior matches the edit, not merely the one with fewest keys.

activities.title: Finish and normalize release metadata
activities.instruction: Append a semicolon to the release row, move down, then uppercase `draft`.

commandGroups.explanation: Append at the first row's line end.
Reach the final word on the next row.
Uppercase that word range.

feedback.success: Both metadata fields now match their target forms.
feedback.why: A chose the punctuation boundary while gUw preserved the word and changed only its case.

provenance.languageRationale: Release metadata naturally combines punctuation and case normalization.

activities.title: Finish and increment a setting
activities.instruction: Append a semicolon, reach the number, then increment it from 2 to 3.

commandGroups.explanation: Append the terminator.
Stand on the number before the terminator.
Increment the number in place.

hints: Finish the line before changing the value.
Move left from the final semicolon.

feedback.success: The setting is terminated and incremented.
feedback.why: A handled the boundary and Ctrl-a preserved the numeric token.

provenance.languageRationale: A small attempt setting naturally combines punctuation and numeric adjustment.

activities.title: Join and normalize a value
activities.instruction: Join the broken assignment, then uppercase `draft`.

commandGroups.explanation: Join and normalize the line boundary.
Reach the joined value.
Uppercase it through the word motion.

hints: Use J followed by a word-sized uppercase transform.

feedback.success: The assignment is joined and normalized.
feedback.why: J repaired structure before gUw changed presentation.

provenance.languageRationale: A broken key/value row combines structural joining with value normalization.

activities.title: Choose the direct entry point
activities.prompt: The cursor is at the start of a long line and a semicolon belongs at its end. Which command begins entry at the right boundary?
activities.explanation: A moves directly to the physical line end and begins appending there.

activities.title: Match the command to the local change
activities.body: You can now enter text at precise boundaries, open rows, correct characters, overwrite spans, inspect history, join lines, transform case, and adjust decimal numbers.
takeaways: Use i, I, a, and A to choose an insertion boundary directly.
Use x, X, r, s, S, or R according to direction and replacement span.
Use u and Ctrl-r to move safely through complete changes.
Choose J or gJ from the desired whitespace policy.
Preserve structure with case and numeric transformations instead of retyping.

reference.purpose: Enter text before or after the cursor, at first text, or at line end.
notes: Uppercase forms include a line-landmark movement.

reference.purpose: Open a new line below or above and enter Insert mode.
notes: Indentation can depend on editor settings.

reference.purpose: Delete under the cursor, delete before it, or replace one character.
Replace a character, a line, or an overwrite stream.
notes: s and S enter Insert mode.
R overwrites until end-of-line, then inserts.

reference.purpose: Undo the latest complete change or redo an undo.
notes: An Insert or Replace session is one history unit.

reference.purpose: Join lines with normalized or preserved boundary whitespace.
notes: J trims indentation and normally inserts one space.

reference.purpose: Toggle a character or transform the case of a motion range.
notes: The g-prefixed forms wait for a motion.

reference.purpose: Increment or decrement the number at or after the cursor.
notes: Prefix with a count to change the amount.
